title: Prime localizations of a quotient of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field are strictly henselian
statement: Let R be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with separably closed fraction field [def-pc-separably-closed], and I an arbitrary ideal. For every prime ideal p of R/I, its prime localization (R/I)_p is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. No properness assumption on I is needed, since the unit quotient has no primes.

source.place: Lemma 09ZC, proof second sentence, using 09Z9 and Algebra Lemma 05WS.

proof.text: Set P = comap of p along the quotient map and A = Localization.AtPrime P. The complement of P contains no zero. Apply isIntegrallyClosed_of_isLocalization and construct the canonical map A to FractionRing R. IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isLocalization shows this is a fraction field of A.

Use the already proved ring-level source theorems HenselianLocalRing.of_isSepClosed_fractionRing and IsLocalRing.isSepClosed_residueField_of_isSepClosed_fractionRing (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.QuasiFinite, the local-domain form of Stacks 09Z9) to build IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing A.

The quotient map is surjective, hence is surjective on prime localizations by RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_surjective. Let phi : A to (R/I)_p be Localization.localRingHom. A unit cannot belong to ker phi since the target is nontrivial, so ker phi lies in the maximal ideal. Apply isStrictlyHenselianLocalRing_quotient with this kernel, retain its strict henselianity conjunct, and transfer it along phi.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective. This avoids explicitly identifying the kernel with I A.
